title: NICD3 mediates pro-angiogenic effects through SMAD3/TGFBI axis in colorectal cancer.
authors: An, Rui; Yu, Ruihao; Wen, Xinxin; Ma, Qingyang; Mao, Kelei; Zhang, Qi; Mao, Liyuan; Feng, Xiaoyan; Xin, Fang; Liu, Ping; Wang, Yijia; Zhang, Jiaqi; Huang, Haixia; Yan, Xiaodong; Wang, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究结直肠癌中NICD3/SMAD3/TGFBI轴促血管生成机制，虽涉及SMAD3与DNA转录激活及分子对接，但核心是信号通路与肿瘤血管生成，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，方法仅简单对接，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: The consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) of colorectal cancer (CRC) represents an aggressive, mesenchymal phenotype associated with the poorest clinical prognosis. Although angiogenesis is fundamental to CRC progression, current anti-VEGF therapies are frequently compromised by primary or acquired resistance, creating an urgent need to identify alternative vascular drivers. NOTCH3 is significantly enriched in CMS4 CRC, yet its direct role in modulating the tumor vasculature remains elusive. Here, integrating multi-center transcriptomic datasets with clinical validation, we identified NOTCH3 as a critical engine of CRC angiogenesis. In Stage IV clinical samples, NOTCH3 expression correlated significantly with microvessel density (MVD). Functionally, overexpression of the NOTCH3 intracellular domain (NICD3) dramatically enhanced endothelial tube formation and migration in vitro, while driving robust tumor vascularization in xenograft models. Through transcriptomic profiling, we identified the secreted factor transforming growth factor-beta-induced protein (TGFBI) as the essential downstream effector. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that NICD3 physically interacts with and upregulates SMAD3, thereby facilitating the direct transcriptional activation of TGFBI. Crucially, to translate these mechanistic insights, we utilized molecular docking and drug screening to identify the flavonoid Hesperidin (HES) as a potent binder of TGFBI. HES treatment effectively abolished NICD3-driven angiogenesis and suppressed tumor progression in vivo. Collectively, our findings characterize a novel NICD3/SMAD3/TGFBI signaling axis as a key vulnerability in CRC and propose HES as a promising precision therapeutic strategy for CRC patients with features of CMS4.
abstract_zh: 结直肠癌（CRC）的共识分子亚型4（CMS4）代表一种侵袭性间充质表型，与最差的临床预后相关。尽管血管生成是CRC进展的基础，但当前抗VEGF疗法常因原发性或获得性耐药而受损，亟需识别替代性血管驱动因子。NOTCH3在CMS4 CRC中显著富集，但其在调节肿瘤血管系统中的直接作用仍不明确。在此，通过整合多中心转录组数据集与临床验证，我们将NOTCH3确定为CRC血管生成的关键引擎。在IV期临床样本中，NOTCH3表达与微血管密度（MVD）显著相关。功能上，NOTCH3胞内域（NICD3）的过表达在体外显著增强内皮细胞管形成和迁移，同时在异种移植模型中驱动强健的肿瘤血管化。通过转录组分析，我们确定分泌因子转化生长因子-β诱导蛋白（TGFBI）为关键下游效应因子。机制上，我们证明NICD3与SMAD3物理相互作用并上调SMAD3，从而促进TGFBI的直接转录激活。关键的是，为转化这些机制见解，我们利用分子对接和药物筛选，鉴定黄酮类化合物橙皮苷（HES）为TGFBI的有效结合剂。HES处理有效消除NICD3驱动的血管生成，并在体内抑制肿瘤进展。总体而言，我们的发现表征了一条新型NICD3/SMAD3/TGFBI信号轴作为CRC的关键脆弱点，并提出HES作为针对具有CMS4特征的CRC患者的精准治疗策略。
